vectors.name: trezor/bitcoin/NFKD-message

key.mnemonic: all all all all all all all all all all all all

vectors.message: Příšerně žluťoučký kůň úpěl ďábelské ódy zákeřný učeň běží podél zóny úlů
vectors.comment: EXPECTED TO DIFFER, THIS IS NORMAL. This message is the same text as the "NFC-message" vector, but written with decomposed Unicode characters (NFKD), e.g. "r" + combining caron instead of "ř". It looks identical on screen but has different bytes (see messageUtf8Hex). Trezor converts messages to NFC before signing, so it signs the same bytes for both vectors and produces the same signature. hw, like Bitcoin Core, signs the exact bytes it is given, so its signature is different. Bitcoin Core's verifymessage rejects Trezor's signature for these bytes. Provenance: Trezor test mnemonic (12 x "all"), no passphrase. Signature converted from hex to base64. Trezor path m/44h/0h/0h/0/1 is hw account 0, chain 0, index 1.

verification.message: Příšerně žluťoučký kůň úpěl ďábelské ódy zákeřný učeň běží podél zóny úlů
verification.comment: EXPECTED TO BE INVALID, THIS IS NORMAL. The same words with their accents decomposed (NFKD). Trezor normalizes a message to NFC before hashing it, so it verifies this spelling too; hw verifies the bytes as given, like Bitcoin Core, and these are the bytes of another message.
